subject: alebrije
pitch:
Category: Fantastical creature.
Subject: alebrije jaguar-eagle.
Style: Oaxacan alebrije painted wood.

spec.name: Alebrije Jaguar-Eagle
spec.description: A Oaxacan alebrije of carved painted wood: a jaguar's body and legs with an eagle's hooked-beak head, crest and spread wings, covered in dot-flower, zigzag and rosette patterns in bright enamel colours.
spec.layout: Rest pose, standing on four paws, facing +Z. The body is a chunky jaguar about 1.9 m long (z -1.0..+0.9), belly at y~0.62 and back at y~1.35. Four sturdy, slightly short jaguar legs with big round paws stand on y=0. Front legs sit at x=±0.30, z~0.6, and hind legs at x=±0.32, z~-0.7 (knee forward, hock back, toe forward). A thick neck rises from the chest forward and up into a big, bold eagle head at about (0,1.6,1.2). The head has an oversized hooked golden beak (upper and lower jaw separate, tip at about z=1.78, y=1.45) and large round eyes with thick dark rims, one on each side. A tall crest of broad feather blades fans up and back from the crown (top y~2.0), with a ruff of overlapping feathers round the neck. The wings are spread wide, almost level, rising slightly to the tips: x out to ±1.85, y 1.2..1.7. Each has a short blocky arm section, covert rows, then layered long flight feathers trailing back (-z) and fanning out to the tip. A long jaguar tail leaves the rump at (0,0.97,-0.95), runs back and sags, then curls up to y~1.3 at z~-1.95 and ends in a fan of 5-7 painted feathers reaching z~-2.25. The look is Oaxacan painted wood: simple chunky carved base shapes, faceted and low-poly, with every surface a flat enamel colour. Detail is made only from small parts seated on the surface: rows of dots, dot-flowers (centre dot, ring of 5-6 petal dots, dark outline disc beneath), jaguar rosettes (dark ring with a coloured centre), zigzag bands, tiny diamonds, spirals and stripes. Every large form gets a contrasting outline colour, a main colour and a fine highlight. All parts share one motif vocabulary: white and yellow dot rows along every edge, magenta, turquoise and cobalt accents against the orange jaguar base, and black outlines. Colour is warm on top and cooler underneath. No ground, base or props.

parts.builds: Torso and neck. The torso is one smooth-skinned loft along hips->spine1->chest, using bone: [hips, spine1, chest]. It runs from the rump at z -1.0 (half-width 0.30, half-height 0.27) to the chest at z +0.85 (half-width 0.38, half-height 0.38), centred around y 0.95-1.05, with belly at y~0.62 and back at y~1.35. Chest and belly are bellyCream, back and flanks jaguarOrange (sectors or bands). A thick neck sweep (bone: [chest, neck1, neck2]) runs from the chest (0,1.08,0.75) through neck1 and neck2 up to the neckTop (0,1.5,1.08), radius 0.27 tapering to 0.22, in jaguarOrange with a cream throat. The head part's ruff covers its end. Painted detail, all as small parts seated on the surface with stick, ring and along: jaguar rosettes (dark ink ring with a magenta, turquoise or yellow centre, 40-60 of them scattered over back and flanks with a minimum spacing); a dorsal stripe of alternating cobalt and magenta diamonds along the spine; rows of white dots round the girth; a zigzag band (turquoise and ink triangles) along each flank; dot-flowers on the shoulders and haunches; a chest bib of 12-16 overlapping rounded feather scales, in rows going lilac/pink/turquoise, on the front of the chest and base of the neck; hip and shoulder 'tattoo' swirls in ink with dot rows. The torso hides the leg-hip sockets and wing roots inside its volume.
parts.attaches: Wings attach at the wingRootL/R mounts (inside the shoulders). Legs attach at hipFL/FR/HL/HR. The tail starts at tailRoot. The neck ends at neckTop, where the head sits. Rides joints hips, spine1, chest, neck1, neck2.

parts.builds: The eagle head, centred on the headCenter mount, built big and bold (head scale about 1.2). The skull is a chunky faceted ellipsoid in jaguarYellow. A cream-and-orange cheek and brow mask surrounds the eyes with a feather pattern. Eyes: two big eyes at x=±0.2, y~1.72, z~1.3 facing sideways and forward, each stacked from an ink disc, a white ring, an eyeGlow iris, an ink pupil and a tiny white highlight, with a thick ink brow ridge above that has three small dots. The beak is built as a separate upper and lower jaw. The upper beak (rides head) is a hooked wedge of beakGold, wide at the base (z 1.35), running forward and curving down to a sharp point at beakTip (0,1.45,1.78), with ink nostril dots, a beakDark ridge line and turquoise/magenta stripe bands. The lower beak (rides jaw) is shorter and lighter, ending around z 1.65, with a red tongue and a cream edge strip inside. A cere of pink and white dots sits at the beak base. The crest is 7-9 broad leaf-shaped feather blades (extrude) fanning up and back from crestRoot (0,1.9,1.05), tallest in the middle (top y~2.0, tilted back), colours cycling magenta, turquoise, cobalt, lime and yellow, with an ink outline blade behind each one, white dot rows on each, and small round tip dots. A neck ruff of 2 rings x 10 overlapping pointed feathers (turquoise, cobalt, pink, white tips) wraps the neck at z 0.95-1.1, around the neckTop mount, leaning back and out. Ear-tuft feathers sit on each side of the crest. Small yellow/white dot garlands run along the beak sides, brows and cheeks.
parts.attaches: Sits on the neck end at neckTop (0,1.5,1.08). The upper beak and skull ride joint head, the lower jaw rides joint jaw (hinge at jawHinge). Nothing hangs in front of the face.

parts.builds: Two spread wings, mirrored (left is +x), each riding wingRoot, wingElbow, wingWrist and wingTip. Each has a chunky arm section (a swept tube of jaguarOrange with rosettes, radius 0.16 tapering to 0.08) from wingRoot through wingElbow and wingWrist to wingTip, with bone: those joints. Behind and under it come feather layers, built as extruded rounded leaf shapes that lie nearly flat and fan out: (1) lesser coverts: 2 rows of short wide feathers along the arm's trailing edge (cobalt, turquoise, magenta); (2) greater coverts: 8-10 medium feathers; (3) 8-9 secondary flight feathers trailing back from the elbow and arm, 0.55-0.75 long, and 7-9 long primaries 0.8-1.0 long fanning back and outward from wrist and tip, with the longest at the tip. Flight feather colours in sequence: magenta, orange, yellow, lime, turquoise, cobalt, purple, each with an ink outline feather slightly larger behind it, a central quill line in white, a row of white dots down the vane, and a contrasting tip band or zigzag. Each feather rides the nearest wing joint. Leading edge: a row of white dots along the front of the arm and a turquoise/ink zigzag band at the wrist. Shoulder cover: a dot-flower of 6 petal dots at each wing root. Wing planes rise gently toward the tips (tip y~1.55) and the feathers droop slightly (a few degrees). Wingspan is ±1.85 in x including feather tips. The wing must clearly clear the torso: the feather trailing edges lie at z -0.2..-1.2.
parts.attaches: Roots at wingRootL/R (±0.32,1.22,0.4), hidden in the shoulders of the body part. Rides wingRoot/Elbow/Wrist/Tip L and R.

parts.builds: Four jaguar legs, mirrored (left is +x), riding hip/knee/ankle/toe F and H, L and R. Front legs: thick swept tubes (radius 0.14 at the top, 0.09 at the wrist) in jaguarOrange with a bellyCream inner side, running hip (y 0.88) -> knee (0.5) -> ankle (0.2) -> toe, ending in big round paws. Hind legs: a heavy thigh (a flattened ellipsoid or loft, radius 0.2) tapering into a bent leg, with the knee forward and the hock back, then a long foot to the toe. Paws are chunky rounded shapes sitting flat on y=0 (lowest points touch the floor), about 0.2 wide and 0.3 long, in jaguarYellow with a cream underside. Each paw has 4 toe bumps in front (spheres) and a gold-white curved claw per toe (small cones, claw colour). Painted detail: ink rosette rings and spots on thighs and shoulders; 2-3 stripes of cobalt/magenta bands (cuffs) with white dot rows round each leg above the paw; a dot-flower on the outer side of each thigh and shoulder; zigzag bands of turquoise and ink on the ankle; a pink pad dot under each paw; a small tuft of 3 pointed feathers at each hock and wrist in turquoise/magenta/white, pointing back.
parts.attaches: Start at the hip mounts hipFL/FR/HL/HR (hidden in the torso). All paw soles rest at y=0. Rides all hip/knee/ankle/toe joints.

parts.builds: A long, thick jaguar tail (a swept tube over tail1..tail4, with bone: [tail1, tail2, tail3, tail4], tapering radius 0.15 -> 0.07) from tailRoot (0,0.97,-0.95) back via (0,0.92,-1.35) and (0,0.95,-1.7), curling up to (0,1.3,-1.95). It is jaguarOrange, with bands (alternating ink and cobalt/magenta rings, one ring per 0.15 m) and a cream underside. Rows of white dots follow the top and the sides, there are a few rosettes at the base, and a dot-flower where it joins the rump. At the end, riding tail4, sits a fan of 5-7 big feathers (extruded leaf blades 0.5-0.7 long) spreading up and back like a peacock plume, the middle one tallest: tipped at z about -2.2 and y up to 1.75, in magenta, turquoise, cobalt, lime, yellow and purple, each with an ink outline feather behind it, a white quill line, rows of dots and a round 'eye' tip (ink disc, white ring, coloured centre). Add a small ruff of 6 short feathers wrapping the tail where the fan meets it. Add a feathered rump-flame crest: 5 small pointed feathers (pink, yellow, orange) along the top of the rump just forward of the tail root at z -0.9..-0.75, y~1.3.
parts.attaches: Starts at the tailRoot mount (0,0.97,-0.95), in the rump of the body part. Rides tail1..tail4.

calls.reasoning:
I'm sketching out the spec for an alebrije jaguar-eagle, starting with its proportions. I'm picturing a jaguar body with eagle wings and head, and I'm settling on a length of about 2.6 along the z axis, a wingspan of roughly 3.0 with the wings extended, and a height near 1.

I'm settling the layout now: the jaguar stands in a quadruped pose with the chest at the front and hips at the back, the neck rising to an eagle head with a hooked beak, the wings spreading out from the shoulders, and the tail curving back from the rump. The overall size comes out to about 3.4 by 1.9 by 3.3, with the wings spanning roughly 1.7 out to each side. I'm also breaking the model into five parts, starting with the torso, which needs painted spots, rosettes, and dotted flower motifs along with its spine and joints.

I'm listing the five parts of the model: body, head, wings, legs, and a tail-and-plumage part that covers the tail chain, feather fan, chest ruff, and leg feathers. Then I'm picking a vivid palette of orange, yellow, black, magenta, turquoise, cobalt, green, red, and white.

I'm working out the joint positions now: the torso sits around y 0.95 and runs along z from about -0.95 to 0.85. The front legs attach at the shoulders and drop to paws on the floor, and the hind legs attach at the hips with the hocks bent back.

Still defining the joint hierarchy, placing the hips, spine, neck, and head positions along the body.

I'm placing the wing joints now: the shoulder sits out from the chest at about x 0.32, with the elbow and wrist stepping outward and back to carry the wing span.

I'm working out the tail placement now, curving it back and up from the rump, and I'm weighing whether the full model length should land near 3.85 along z to fit the tail tip.

I'm laying out the tail's joints, curving it back and up to a plume tip near z -2.2, which puts the model's total length at about 4.0 and its size at roughly 3.7 by 2.0 by 4.0. I'm now working out how to name the leg chains, weighing whether to keep the front legs as separate front-left and front-right chains so they don't clash with the wing names.

I'm now placing the leg joints for the front legs: a hip at the shoulder area around x 0.3, y 0.85, z 0.55, then a knee and ankle stepping down toward the floor, with the toe last.

I'm continuing to lay out the leg joints, with a hip, knee, ankle, and toe for each front and hind leg.

I'm now fixing the bounding boxes: the torso runs from about y 0.55 to 1.4 and z -1.0 to 0.9, with its belly near y 0.62 and the legs hipping in at 0.85. The head box sits roughly from y 1.3 to 2.0 and z 1.0 to 1.8, while the neck tube belongs to the body and extends up to the head joint.

I'm placing the wing roots at about x 0.32 and sweeping the wing elbow and wrist outward, with the tips lifted slightly so the wings read as extended rather than drooping.

I'm setting the wing joint's tip and direction, then splitting the remaining parts so the chest bib goes with the tail and plumage rather than the head.

I'm now sizing the model's parts against a total budget of about 890 units, setting the body at 210, the head at 210, the wings at 220, the legs at 150, and the tail at 100. I'm also working out where the neck's top joint should sit so it meets the head cleanly.

I'm placing the torso's loft stations along z, with the rump near z -1.0 and the chest near z 0.7, widening and rising slightly toward the front so the belly sits around y 0.62 and the hips are covered.

I'm now fixing the head's details: an eagle head with a hooked beak, a yellow beak with magenta and turquoise stripes, and eyes set at the sides with rings around them. I'm also setting the jaw's hinge at the back of the head so it can open.

I'm weighing how the builders will find the joints by name, and whether they can look them up through the builder object or need them passed in directly.

Now I'm setting the joint orientations, starting with the hips and a downward direction for the spine.

Still writing out the joint list: the hips, spine, chest, and neck joints are each placed along the body with their parent and direction, and I'm now working on the head joint at the base of the skull.

I'm placing the jaw joint at the cheek, around z 1.12, so the lower beak hinges there, and I'm setting the tail chain as four joints curving back and down from the hips toward the plume tip.

I'm finishing the tail joints and placing the fan feathers on the last tail joint. Then I'm laying out the left wing chain from the root out through the elbow, wrist, and tip, with the right wing mirrored.

I'm finalizing the joint list and counting it: seven for the spine, neck, head, and jaw, then four for the tail, eight for the wings, and sixteen for the legs, which brings it to about 35. I'm also checking that the wing roots sit just inside the torso surface, and that the leg parts and floor contact are set.

Next I'm choosing a palette of about twenty colors and working out the mounts. The surfaces will all get dot, zigzag, and flower decoration, built around a dot-flower motif with a yellow center, a ring of magenta and turquoise petals, and a black outline. I'm also writing the JSON.
